# dsh-turn-badge
English | 简体中文

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that treats a
finished turn the way Codex does: **a native notification, a

n app-icon badge and a title dot**,
cleared the moment you come back.
> Community plugin. Not affiliated with or maintained by DeepSeek AI.
## The problem

Harness runs long tasks. When you switch to another window, finishing the task changes a dot
inside

a sidebar you are not looking at. Nothing reaches the operating system, so there is no
notification,
no taskbar/Dock badge and no reason to notice — until you remember to check.
## What it does
A turn is "finished" when its session goes from **running** to **idle**.

- **Native notification** — title + session title, e.g. *Task finished — "Weekly report"*.
Clicking

focuses the app and opens that session when the workspace service is available.
- **App-icon badge**

— unread session count on the app icon via the Badging API
(`setAppBadge`), plus the browser tab ba

dge (`setClientBadge`) where supported.
- **Title dot** — a `● ` prefix on the window/tab title, so

there is always a visible fallback.
- **Clear on focus** — returning to the window clears the badge,
the title marker and the toast.

It stays quiet when you are already looking at the session that finished, skips subagent
sessions by
default, and counts distinct sessions rather than turns.

## Configure
Settings live in `localStorage`; change them from the DevTools console and refresh:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. `false` disables the whole plugin. |
| `toast` | `true` | OS n

otification. |
| `badge` | `true` | Badging API calls (app icon and tab). |
| `titleDot` | `true` |

`● ` title marker. |
| `notifyWhenFocusedOtherSession` | `true` | Alert when the app is focused but

another session is open. |
| `skipSubagents` | `true` | Do not notify for subagent sessions. |
Reset with `localStorage.removeItem('dsh-turn-badge.settings')`.

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- The client half subscribes to `ctx.uiSession.sessionStatus`, the per-session
`{ running, pendingIn

teraction, completionUnread }` snapshot the Harness client already
maintains. It records a baseline

at load and acts only on a real **true → false** transition.
- The session title comes from the clie

nt's session list; no transcript is read.
- The host half is intentionally empty. It exists so the p

ackage becomes an active Loader row,
which is what makes `dsh-client-modules` publish the client bun

dle.
- No HTTP endpoint, no model calls, no network traffic.
## Platform support
Everything is standard web API, with no Windows- or macOS-specific code:
| Capability | Windows | macOS |

| Native notification | Notification Center | Notification Center |
| App-icon badge | Badging API (

installed PWA / capable Chromium carrier) | Badging API (capable Chromium / Safari carrier) |
| Tab

badge | Chromium `setClientBadge` | Chromium `setClientBadge` |
| Title dot | every carrier | every

hromium `setClientBadge` | Chromium `setClientBadge` |
| Title dot | every carrier | every carrier |

**Honest limitation:** in the DSH desktop app the taskbar/Dock badge depends on Electron's
support f

or the Badging API. A page plugin cannot call the Electron main process directly. When
the badge is

unsupported, the notification and the title dot still work; in an installed PWA the
badge is at its

ported, the notification and the title dot still work; in an installed PWA the
badge is at its best.
## Privacy

- No telemetry, analytics or remote requests.
- Reads only session status and session **titles**, ne

ver message bodies or tool output.
- The settings key is the only thing written to `localStorage`.
-
Notification bodies are rendered locally by the OS.
See SECURITY.md for the full threat model.
## Compatibility

- Harness `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.2.3-0`; verified on `0.2.2-rc.1` with the desktop profile.
- `web` and `d

esktop` profiles.
- Requires the `uiSession` and `sessions` client services (part of the standard we

profiles.
- Requires the `uiSession` and `sessions` client services (part of the standard web app).
## Limitations

- **Badge support is environmental** — see the platform table above.
- **The page must be alive.** A

desktop window in the tray still notifies; a browser tab frozen
by the OS may delay it.
- **Failure

and success look the same.** Any running → idle transition is reported as finished.
- **Subagents a

re skipped by default**; enable them with `skipSubagents: false`.
- **The title marker is reapplied*

* when the shell rewrites `document.title`, so it can flicker
for a frame during navigation.
## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Check |
| No notification | Allow notifications for the app; check Do Not Disturb; try `__dshTurnBadge.previ

ew()` |
| No red dot | The carrier does not implement the Badging API — use an installed PWA or rely

on the title dot |
| Nothing at all | Restart Harness; the host reads the profile at boot. Check th

e browser console for `[dsh-turn-badge]` |
| Notified twice | Two sessions finished; the badge count

s distinct sessions, not turns |
| Title dot disappeared | Another plugin overwrote the title; the o
bserver re-adds it on the next change |
